title: Naperville Smart Thermostat Rebates 2026: City $75 and Nicor Gas $25
desc: Naperville smart thermostat rebates in 2026: the city's electric utility pays $75 for up to two thermostats per household, and Nicor Gas pays $25 or a bundle with a furnace. ComEd does not apply.
lead: In Naperville you can collect from two different companies for a smart thermostat. The City of Naperville's electric utility pays $75, and you can claim it for up to two thermostats. Nicor Gas, your gas company, pays $25 for one if your home heats with gas. ComEd's thermostat rebate is not for Naperville customers. Here are the rules we read on October 6, 2026.
cards_intro: The two rebates come from two separate programs with separate forms.

cards.title: Naperville Electric smart thermostat
cards.note: Any Wi-Fi smart thermostat that you can adjust from a phone. Owners and renters can apply.

cards.title: Nicor Gas smart thermostat
cards.note: One per household, on a home with a gas furnace or boiler, and the thermostat must be on Nicor's approved list or ENERGY STAR certified.

cards.title: Nicor furnace and thermostat bundle
cards.note: A 95% or 97% efficient furnace with a smart thermostat on the same application.

cards.title: Naperville rebates now closed
cards.note: Attic, window, tune-up and blower motor rebates are used up this year.

after_cards: Naperville's page does not say that you must give to its Renewable Energy Program for the thermostat rebate, unlike the attic and window rebates.
sections: You buy and install any smart thermostat with Wi-Fi that lets you change the temperature from afar. The city says all makes and models are included. You then fill out an application in the city's online portal, which needs an account, and attach your receipt and proof of install. A one-time $75 credit appears on your electric bill within two months. The complete application must reach the city within 120 days of installation. Funding is first-come, and the program ends when it is gone.

Nicor's thermostat must be installed on a home with a gas furnace or boiler of home size. It needs a working Wi-Fi connection and features such as geofencing, which uses your phone's location to adjust the heat when you leave. A smart thermostat can replace a manual or programmable one, but not another smart thermostat. Nicor says a rebate from your electric company does not block the Nicor one. Apply within 90 days of install or by January 31, 2027.

The Census Bureau's survey for 2020 to 2024 counts 54,847 households in Naperville. Owners are 74.8% and renters 25.2%. Utility gas heats 86.1% of homes, which means most households can use the Nicor rebate, and electricity heats 11.9%, for whom the city's rebate is the main one. Detached houses are 62.8% of homes.

The city lets you claim two. That helps in a two-story house with two zones, or in a house with an addition. Nicor allows only one per household, so the second thermostat would earn only the city's $75.

A smart thermostat saves energy only if you use its schedule. Ask the installer to set an away temperature and a night setback, and to show you how to change them from your phone. Keep the box and the model number, because Nicor's form asks for them. If you plan a heat pump, ask whether the thermostat you pick works with it, because some thermostats do not control heat pumps well.
claim_heading: How to get a thermostat rebate in Naperville
claim_steps: Check that your electric bill comes from the City of Naperville and your gas from Nicor Gas.
Buy a smart thermostat with Wi-Fi from a store or an installer.
Keep the receipt and a photo of the installed unit.
Apply to the city within 120 days and to Nicor within 90 days.
Wait for the credit on your electric bill and the Nicor card or check.

faq: How much does Naperville pay for a smart thermostat?
$75, with a limit of two rebates per household.
Does ComEd pay for a thermostat in Naperville?
No. Naperville's electric company is the city, and ComEd's rebate is for ComEd customers.
Can I get Nicor and the city rebate on the same thermostat?
Both programs are separate, and Nicor's page says an electric company rebate does not block its own. Check each program's terms before you apply.
120 days after installation for the city and 90 days for Nicor, or January 31, 2027, whichever comes first.
Yes for the city rebate. Nicor's thermostat is for gas customers, and a landlord can apply.
